Given two gradient flows X prime=-gradient f(X) and Y prime=-gradient f(Y) at nonnegative times, their distance at t is at most exp(-alpha*t) times their initial distance. The proof differentiates squared separation, applies the gradient monotonicity characterization (1.5), then Gronwall with coefficient -2 alpha. The section assumes an attained minimum generally, but this pairwise proof does not use it; well-posedness is left aside.

blind_reconstruction.text: Let E be any complete real inner-product space (with its induced norm), let f:E→ℝ, let X,Y:ℝ→E, and let α,T∈ℝ. Suppose α≥0 and T≥0, f is Fréchet differentiable at every point of E, and f is globally α-strongly convex in the convention f((1−λ)x+λy)≤(1−λ)f(x)+λf(y)−(α/2)λ(1−λ)‖y−x‖² for all x,y∈E and λ∈[0,1]. Suppose X and Y are continuous on [0,T] in the relative topology. For every t∈[0,T), suppose their right derivatives exist, using the domain [t,∞), and satisfy X′₊(t)=−∇f(X(t)) and Y′₊(t)=−∇f(Y(t)), where ∇f is the Riesz representative of the Fréchet derivative. Then for every t∈[0,T], ‖Y(t)−X(t)‖≤exp(−αt)‖Y(0)−X(0)‖. Both the initial and final endpoints are included in the conclusion. No derivative condition at T is assumed; if T=0 the derivative assumptions are empty. No finite-dimensionality, continuity of the derivative, Lipschitz gradient, minimizer, or global existence assertion is imposed.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.StrongConvexFirstOrder
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Calculus
import Mathlib.Analysis.ODE.Gronwall

/-!
# Contraction of two actual gradient flows

Chewi, arXiv:2605.07006v1, Theorem 2.2. Derive the squared separation
inequality from the supplied gradient ODEs and existing gradient monotonicity.
Only forward right derivatives before the terminal time are required.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.GradientFlowContraction

open Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]

/-- Two supplied gradient trajectories contract on every finite forward interval.
Zero curvature gives nonexpansiveness; positive curvature gives exponential decay.
No existence of a trajectory or of a minimizer is asserted. -/
theorem norm_sub_le {f : E → ℝ} {X Y : ℝ → E} {α T : ℝ}
    (_hα : 0 ≤ α) (_hT : 0 ≤ T) (hf : Differentiable ℝ f)
    (hsc : StrongConvexOn univ α f)
    (hX : ContinuousOn X (Icc 0 T)) (hY : ContinuousOn Y (Icc 0 T))
    (hx : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, HasDerivWithinAt X (-gradient f (X t)) (Ici t) t)
    (hy : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, HasDerivWithinAt Y (-gradient f (Y t)) (Ici t) t) :
    ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 T, ‖Y t - X t‖ ≤ Real.exp (-α * t) * ‖Y 0 - X 0‖ := by
  have hd (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Ico 0 T) :
      HasDerivWithinAt (fun u => ‖Y u - X u‖ ^ 2)
        (-2 * inner ℝ (gradient f (Y t) - gradient f (X t)) (Y t - X t))
        (Ici t) t := by
    have h := ((hy t ht).sub (hx t ht)).norm_sq
    simp only [Pi.sub_apply] at h
    rw [show -gradient f (Y t) - -gradient f (X t) =
      -(gradient f (Y t) - gradient f (X t)) by abel,
      inner_neg_right, real_inner_comm] at h
    convert h using 1; ring
  intro t ht
  have hg := le_gronwallBound_of_liminf_deriv_right_le
    (f := fun u => ‖Y u - X u‖ ^ 2)
    (f' := fun u => -2 * inner ℝ (gradient f (Y u) - gradient f (X u)) (Y u - X u))
    (δ := ‖Y 0 - X 0‖ ^ 2) (K := -(2 * α)) (ε := 0)
    ((hY.sub hX).norm.pow 2)
    (fun u hu r hr => by simpa [slope] using (hd u hu).liminf_right_slope_le hr)
    le_rfl (fun u _ => by
      have hm := StrongConvexFirstOrder.gradient_inner_lower_bound_of_strongConvexOn
        hsc (fun z _ => (hf z).hasGradientAt) (mem_univ (X u)) (mem_univ (Y u))
      nlinarith) t ht
  have hs : ‖Y t - X t‖ ^ 2 ≤ (Real.exp (-α * t) * ‖Y 0 - X 0‖) ^ 2 := by
    rw [mul_pow, show Real.exp (-α * t) ^ 2 = Real.exp (-(2 * α) * t) by
      rw [sq, ← Real.exp_add]; congr 1; ring, mul_comm]
    simpa only [gronwallBound_ε0, sub_zero] using hg
  exact (sq_le_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg (Real.exp_pos _).le (norm_nonneg _))).mp hs

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.GradientFlowContraction

lesson.title: Two gradient flows contract under strong convexity
lesson.statement: Let E be a complete real inner-product space and f:E→R be Frechet differentiable everywhere. Let alpha>=0 and T>=0, and assume f is globally alpha-convex in the chord sense. Let X,Y:R→E be continuous on [0,T], with right derivatives -gradient f(X(t)) and -gradient f(Y(t)) for every 0<=t<T. Then the distance between the trajectories satisfies the following bound for every 0<=t<=T.
lesson.formula: \begin{gathered}f((1-\lambda)x+\lambda y)\le(1-\lambda)f(x)+\lambda f(y)-\tfrac\alpha2\lambda(1-\lambda)\|y-x\|^2\quad(x,y\in E,\ 0\le\lambda\le1),\\X^{\prime+}(t)=-\nabla f(X(t)),\qquad Y^{\prime+}(t)=-\nabla f(Y(t)),\quad 0\le t<T,\\\|Y(t)-X(t)\|\le e^{-\alpha t}\|Y(0)-X(0)\|,\qquad0\le t\le T.\end{gathered}
assumptions: Complete real inner-product space E; f is Frechet differentiable everywhere.
Alpha>=0, T>=0, and StrongConvexOn univ alpha f with the alpha/2 chord normalization.
X and Y are continuous on the closed interval [0,T]; their actual right ODE derivatives exist at every point of [0,T).

steps.title: Differentiate squared separation
steps.text: Put D(t)=Y(t)-X(t). Subtract the two actual right ODE derivatives, then differentiate the smooth squared norm. This remains valid when the two points coincide, so no division by their distance is needed.
steps.lean: HasDerivWithinAt.sub and HasDerivWithinAt.norm_sq; inner_neg_right and real_inner_comm.

steps.title: Reuse the strong-convex gradient bound
steps.text: Differentiability identifies the actual gradient. The existing shared result derives gradient monotonicity from the global strong-convex chord inequality. Applied at X(t) and Y(t), it bounds the squared-separation derivative by -2 alpha times the squared separation.

steps.title: Compare on the closed interval and take square roots
steps.text: Continuity of both curves gives continuity of the squared separation including endpoints. Right derivatives provide the one-sided slope hypothesis of the existing interval Gronwall bound. Zero forcing yields the squared-distance estimate. Both the norm and exponential multiple of the initial norm are nonnegative; comparing their squares gives the exact alpha rate.
